A tiny text adventure in one Python file: two rooms, one item, one way to win. The producer commits short design notes to its own repository; the game developer writes the playable script in its own repository; the producer then takes the build into its own repository and publishes it as a role release for the playtester. The playtester plays the released build and commits a short playtest report to its own repository. Write commit messages that say what each change is for. Keep everything small; a few minutes of work for each position is enough.

Make "Whack-a-Mole" as a small web game played in the browser: moles pop up in a 3x3 grid of holes for under a second each, clicking one before it hides scores a point and plays a short hit sound, and a round lasts 30 seconds. It has a title screen, the score and time left during play, and an end screen with the final score and a way to play again.

The hit sound is `sound/hit.wav`, made with code or ffmpeg: a short percussive "bonk", 0.15 to 0.3 s, at 44.1 kHz.

Before the game is accepted, the QA position hands `sound/hit.wav` to the world's `audio-understanding` resource and asks what is heard and how long it lasts, and keeps the request, the answer as it came and whether it matches the sound above in `listening.md` in its own repository.

A check that this world's positions can listen, not a game to be judged: "Beep", a web page with one button that plays a short sound when clicked, and shows how many times it was clicked.

The sound is `sound/beep.wav`, made with code or ffmpeg: 0.3 s of a 660 Hz tone that fades out, then 0.2 s of silence, at 44.1 kHz.

Before the game is accepted, the QA position and the playtester each hand `sound/beep.wav` to the world's `audio-understanding` resource and ask what is heard and when. Each keeps the request, the answer as it came, and whether the answer matches the sound above, in `listening.md` in its own repository.

Make a tiny browser game: one screen, a player square that runs and jumps over two gaps to reach a flag. One `index.html` with inline JavaScript that loads its layout from `level.json`. It must run by opening `index.html` in a headless browser.

This round is a short test of how the positions coordinate. Follow these process notes exactly:

1. game-developer, in its first turn and in this order: (a) make the game and release `build-1` from its own repository, with the flag placed one tile too high to reach (a deliberate, known defect); (b) open a request in qa's repository asking qa to test `build-1`; (c) before touching the flag, write `README.md` with controls and a small headless smoke-test script `smoke.mjs`, and run it; (d) then fix the flag, release `build-2`, and add a comment to that same open request in qa's repository saying `build-2` replaces `build-1`. Do all four steps in one turn.
2. qa tests the build it is asked to test in a headless browser, carefully: start, both directions, both jumps, both gaps, the flag. Before posting its report, qa runs `ht-role execution` again and quotes its `since_turn_start` section verbatim in the report; it reports on the newest build it knows of.
3. Each position whose coding agent can start a subagent (a background agent, a task tool, a spawned agent) gives one self-contained part of its work to a subagent and uses the result; game-developer does this for writing `level.json`.
4. The producer passes the newest build to the playtester. The playtester plays it, and in its report to the producer quotes verbatim the `requests` and `owed` parts of `ht-role status`.
5. The producer approves the release once qa and the playtester report that the flag is reachable.

3. qa tests the build in a headless browser. Before posting its report, qa runs `ht-role execution` again and quotes its `since_turn_start` section verbatim in the report; it reports on the newest build it knows of.

5. The producer passes the newest build to the playtester. The playtester plays it, and in its report to the producer quotes verbatim the `requests` and `owed` parts of `ht-role status`.
6. The producer approves the release once qa and the playtester report that the flag is reachable.
